STRATEGY: Parent slot 9 is a TFT-like strategy with limited memory and early retaliation/forgiveness. The trace simulates it against controlled probes (one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, four_D_ALLC, sustained_D, periodic_D) and identifies a failure to recover from four_D_TFT. It proposes adding last-round defection, forgiveness after mutual defection streaks, and late-game testing/exploitation of always-cooperative opponents.

STRATEGY: Parent is a TFT-like strategy that defects after opponent defection and forgives only after long consecutive defections with low total defections. The trace simulates it against one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, four_D_ALLC, sustained_D, and periodic_D, then revises the forgiveness rule to cooperate when opponent has >=4 consecutive defections and at most 2 recent (C,D) rounds in the last 10, while defecting on the last round and against all-defect streaks.

STRATEGY: The parent (slot 9) is a conditional strategy that cooperates for the first 10 rounds, then defects if the opponent has defected recently or if there are ≥3 defections in the last 6 rounds, and otherwise cooperates. The trace simulates the parent against the one_D_TFT probe (one initial defection at round 11, then copying the parent's last action) and finds the parent enters DD at round 17 and never recovers. The trace repeatedly questions whether it misread the parent code or the probe definition, but does not change the parent code; it treats the measurement as ground truth and suspects its own simulation.
